pages.title: Overall XP Attribute
pages.text: Add a mastery:attribute skill effect targeting mastery:experience_gain. It starts at 1. An add_value amount of 0.2 adds 20 percentage points per active rank. Classes can grant the same attribute through their Attributes list.

pages.title: A Specific Tree
pages.text: Bundled trees have attributes such as mastery:fire_experience_gain and mastery:flame_blade_experience_gain. These also start at 1. Overall and tree attributes multiply together. Attribute values are bounded from 0 to 100; zero disables earned XP for that scope.

pages.title: Any Data-defined Tree
pages.text: Use the mastery:experience_gain effect for a tree added by your datapack. Set Tree to the desired tree ID and Amount to a fraction, such as 0.25 for 25% per active rank. Reset Tree or leave it empty to affect all trees. This effect does not require registering a new attribute.

pages.title: Combining Skill Effects
pages.text: Matching mastery:experience_gain amounts add after rank scaling. The final factor is 1 plus that sum, limited to 0 through 101. Disabled or unavailable skills contribute nothing. This factor multiplies both the overall and tree XP attributes.

pages.title: Choose an XP Attribute
pages.text: A tree's Xp attribute field can select another already registered multiplier attribute. For example, mastery:fire_experience_gain lets a custom tree share Fire's bonus. Leaving it empty uses the bundled matching attribute, or 1 for an unknown custom tree. Reload cannot create new attributes.

pages.title: What Changes
pages.text: Gameplay XP sources and MasteryAPI.grantXp apply these modifiers once. Direct points, Minecraft XP, and purchase costs are unaffected. /mastery xp add stays exact for administration. Existing level caps still apply; a once-only source is not replayed when bonuses change later.

pages.title: Skill Damage XP
pages.text: Unlocked, enabled skills award XP to their own tree from damage dealt, regardless of damage type. Skill damage xp defaults to 1 per damage and can be overridden on trees or nodes; zero disables it. Normal damage XP sources run first. This supplies XP only if they did not credit the skill’s tree. Other trees and kill rewards still work normally.
